title: The Clinic slice
goal: A crew of up to four rides the elevator into a bright two-level Clinic floor, finds the Orderly, takes a reading, and banks or rides down.
nowText: An Opus agent is building the earning rule as tested logic: the instrument only records while the Orderly is moving near you, which means while nobody is looking at it.

tasks.title: Project setup
tasks.why: The tools that build, test and publish the game, and the live link.
tasks.summary: Typecheck, 7 rule tests and the build pass. The browser test boots the game on this PC's graphics card and its screenshot was looked at. CI and a secret scan run on every push.

tasks.title: The Clinic floor generator
tasks.why: Every floor is built from a seed, so every player gets the same building and no two runs match.
tasks.summary: 29 tests pass over 800 generated floors (200 seeds at four depths): every room reachable from the elevator, two levels joined by a stair, an atrium, dead-end side branches, a corridor loop and long sight lines. Fable re-ran the checks and read a printed map.

media.caption: Printed map of one floor, lower then upper level

tasks.title: Walking through a floor
tasks.why: The first time the game is a place you can move around in, in first person.
tasks.summary: You can walk a generated two-level Clinic floor in first person: corridors, rooms with door gaps, a stair, and a balcony over the atrium. 48 rule tests pass, including collision. A browser test walks from the elevator up the stair to the balcony, and a second one presses real keys: W walks, Shift creeps, a wall stops you. Fable re-ran everything and looked at the screenshots. Lighting is flat and the rooms are empty; mouse look is not tested.

tasks.title: The Orderly, second pass
tasks.why: The first entity. The first pass reads as a mannequin; this pass has to make it frightening in bright light.

media.caption: First pass, as a player would meet it
First pass poses: idle, walk, walk, reach, frozen
First pass at game resolution: the smile is lost

Orderly second pass, rounds 1 to 4: now 2.67 m tall (the door beside it is 2.1 m), thin body with knobbly knees and elbows, a bare bony left shoulder, darker gown so it stands out against the white walls, and a much bigger printed smile
Close-up: above the mask there are no eyes, only two sunken dark sockets sewn shut with a few stitches. The printed grin now covers the whole mask in a thick black line

Poses: idle, two frames of the heavy stepped walk (the head stays level), the reach with the arm stretching longer than an arm should, folding to fit under a 2.1 m door frame with the arms hanging, and the frozen pose
From the horror-character tutorial by David Kohlmann: the eye socket built as rings of edges stepping back into the skull. The Orderly's sealed eye sockets are built the same way, in script
In the game at 4 m: the Orderly in the real Clinic with its own shadow on the floor; the printed grin and the two dark sockets read at the game's resolution
In the game beside a 2.1 m door frame: its head is well above the top of the frame, so it has to fold to get through
In the game at 16 m: a thin dark figure with a pale face patch at the end of the hall. At 40 m it shrinks to a dark sliver about 13 pixels tall and the face is lost
Second pass standing in the game at 4 metres, with a real shadow
The problem to fix: at 40 metres it is a sliver you cannot pick out
Second pass face: sewn-shut sockets and a bolder printed smile

Round 1 fixes: new waiting posture (hunched at the top of the back, knees soft, head pushed forward and tilted, one foot turned out, long hands folded at the chest with elbows out), a thinner and much wider printed grin, bigger dark sewn sockets, real knees and long-toed bare feet, a hospital gown with a cross print, a wristband, an uneven hem and trailing ties
Round 1 fixes in the game at 4 m: shaded like the room, lighter tones, less grain, and its shadow is now a soft pool directly under its feet
Round 1 fixes in the game at 40 m (enlarged crop): the elbows standing out make it a figure rather than a post even at about 14 pixels tall
Round 1 fixes, poses: waiting, heavy walk with one hand lifted, the reach now a low palm-up offer of help with the arm still lengthening, folding through a 2.1 m door, frozen with a beckoning hand

Round 2 fixes: the black eye holes are gone. The lids are closed and sewn with thick, uneven stitches, one sunk deeper than the other. The skin is waxy yellow-white, the cap is a puffy crinkled paper bouffant, and the mask is a blue pleated surgical mask with ear loops, a damp yellowed patch and a printed grin that runs off its edges

Round 2 fixes in the game: pale flesh and washed blue paper in the corridor's light, lit from above, with a short contact shadow the feet stand in; shoulders hiked to the ears, head dropped further forward
Round 2 fixes, poses: knobbed knees, elbows and wrists with the limbs tapering between them, arched feet on their toes, and a reach where only the forearm lengthens and the elbow stays bent
Final round, in the game at 4 metres: pale skin, paper cap, hands folded like staff waiting to help
Final round face: lids sewn shut, and the printed smile runs off the mask
Final round at about 15 metres down a corridor
Final round poses: idle, walk, reach, the doorway duck, frozen

tasks.summary: The Orderly was rebuilt after tutorial study and three judged rounds. It is a rigged 2.6 m figure with five animations (idle, walk, reach, a duck under door frames, frozen), it stands in the game with a real shadow, and all checks pass. It is now its own character: pale waxy skin, lids sewn shut, a paper cap, hands folded like staff waiting to help. Honest result: five blind judges scored it 3 to 6 out of 10 for fear and the scores did not rise across rounds. A question about what to do next is waiting for you.

tasks.summary: The game now looks like worn videotape: smeared colour, grain, glaring ceiling lights, a slight wobble, rare tracking rolls, and a PLAY display with a running counter. ?fx=0 turns it off and ?fx=2 makes it heavy. ?debug=1 adds a minimap. Frame time stays at the screen's refresh rate at all three levels, including a phone-sized view and the 8-bit path older phones use. Fable switched the effect off on purpose and confirmed the test fails. Judged from stills only: how the wobble feels in motion over a long session is unverified.

tasks.title: Stronger checks
tasks.why: So a regression is caught by a machine, not by luck: reference screenshots that fail the test when the picture changes, a frame-time limit inside the browser test, a smoke test for the hub, and a deliberate-break check on every gate already passed.
tasks.summary: Four new safety nets. Reference pictures of three views fail the test if the scenery changes: after tightening, a 4% pink tint on the corridor walls and doors 10 cm taller are both caught, and unchanged scenery passes three runs in a row. A frame-time limit of 20 ms is enforced in three situations, including the Orderly on screen and the heavy tape level at 1080p. A hub smoke test checks its pages answer and ten path-escape attempts are refused, on every commit. The floor generator's tests were proven able to fail by removing its stairs. Reference pictures and the frame limit run on this PC only; CI draws in software and skips them.

tasks.summary: The Orderly now hunts you in the game. It walks the floor while nobody is looking, stops the instant you look (checked on every drawn frame, so a quick glance counts), and its trolley squeak plays in 3D while it moves and cuts out within a tenth of a second when it freezes. Being caught is a placeholder: interference, then you are back at the elevator. A browser test plays the staring contest: 3 seconds watched with no movement and no sound, turn away and it closes in, turn back and it is frozen nearer, mid-step. Fable also made it count as its full drawn size for being seen, arms and cap included; a first attempt at that broke the rule and the independent checker caught it. Nobody has heard the squeak yet: neither the agent nor Fable can hear.

gates.title: Builds clean from a fresh clone
Floors are sound
gates.evidence: 800 floors checked by test; one printed map read by eye. Deliberate break used: with stairs removed from the generator, 2 of its 21 tests fail.

gates.title: The Orderly is a real figure
gates.evidence: A re-runnable Blender script builds a rigged figure (7,380 triangles, 39 bones, 5 animations) that loads, animates and casts a shadow in the game; Fable looked at renders and in-game screenshots; five blind critics over three rounds, worst findings fixed each round. Deliberate break used: with the model file hidden, the Orderly browser test fails. Not claimed: that it is frightening. Blind fear scores stayed between 3 and 6 out of 10.

media.caption: The Orderly in the game

gates.title: Heard before seen
gates.evidence: In 104 generated layouts the squeak is audible at least 2.5 seconds before the figure could first be seen, and in the running game the squeak gain is zero while it is watched and rises when it moves. Deliberate break used: with its hearing range cut to 3 metres, the heard-before-seen test fails. The sound itself has not been heard by a person.

The Orderly's rule is proven in logic: across 500 simulated runs an independent checker looked at 48,226 moments when a player could see it, and it had not moved in any of them. It moved in 498 runs and caught someone in 150, so the test is not empty. In 104 layouts its squeak could be heard at least 2.5 seconds before it could be seen. Fable broke the rule two ways on purpose (a too-narrow idea of 'seen', and no grace period) and the checker caught both.
